detail.longDescription: I like using Claude to explain stuff to me when I'm learning something new. Faster than duckduckgoing it. Like "explain how into() works in Rust" or "explain how to launch a subprocess". I could of course just tell it to "build me my tool", but that's not much fun. In this case I've long wanted a tool that can monitor callbacks triggered by GitHub when something is pushed to a repo/branch. The tool should then proceed to update the local copy, build it and then deploy it locally. Pretty trivial, but saves a fair deal of time on development setups where you basically want to rebuild on every single push. I built a tool like that in Python for another (now defunct) project, but it's not open source and I don't think I can use it directly. So this is a good reason to build something new and get better up to speed with Rust. # rust # github # deployment
